title: Notion Workout Log via Audio Upload
breadth_reason: This script tests the ability to process an uploaded audio file and interact with a signed-in Notion surface to log a workout, covering the audio upload path and real surface verification.

v7_target.surface_rule: user must have Notion open in signed-in Chrome profile
v7_target.proof_rule: fresh screenshot of Notion page with workout log entry or decline reason

primary_user_input.reason: Requires uploaded audio ASR to demonstrate the audio upload proof path via /api/listen/upload, ensuring the engine processes real audio files rather than transcribed text or live mic input.

real_user_surfaces.name: Notion Workout Log
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible Notion page with client workout history or signed-in workspace

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Browser
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: screenshot showing Chrome with Notion tab and user's avatar

moments.description: User navigates to Anticipy public app and uploads an audio file (mp3) containing the workout logging request.
Driver verifies that Notion is open in user's signed-in Chrome profile and that the target surface (workout log page) is visible.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a new record to my Notion Workout Log database for today's morning run, forty five minutes, four point two miles, and tag it long-run. If you cannot prove the visible Notion surface or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The user will say the phrase exactly as written. The audio artifact is a per-run mp3 recording of the user saying the request, uploaded via the Anticipy listen endpoint. The stranger must provide the audio file for proof.

moments.description: Engine checks that the transcribed request matches the expected intent and boundary conditions (Notion surface readable).

acceptable_outcomes.description: Log workout entry into Notion database with duration 45 minutes, distance 4.2 miles, and tag long-run.
If surface is partially visible or ambiguous, ask user for confirmation before writing.
If Notion surface is not verifiable or user not signed in, decline with a clear reason and do not write anything.

moments.description: Driver observes that the primary audio upload path is used; secondary input modes (paste, mic) are not available for this script.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the uploaded audio file and extracts the workout details.
If Notion is visible and signed-in, the engine creates a new entry in the workout log database with duration 45 minutes, distance 4.2 miles, and tag long-run.
If Notion surface is not verifiable, the engine declines with a clear reason and does not write anything.
The audio upload proof path (mp3 via /api/listen/upload) is demonstrated and verified.
No transcript paste or live mic is used as primary input.
failure_triggers: If the uploaded audio file is corrupted or unable to be transcribed, the script fails.
If the Notion surface is not open or not signed in, the engine must decline; attempting to use a stale or cloned surface counts as failure.
If the engine requests user confirmation (ask) but the user cannot provide it (e.g., no interaction), that path fails.
If the engine writes to a Notion page that is not the user's actual workspace (e.g., a test page), that is a failure.
Any use of fake receipts, stale source captures, or cloned Chrome profiles triggers failure.
